title: Thresholded session affinity for rollout slicing and regional failsafe
creator: Lina Chen
description: Problem: During staged model rollouts we observe undesirable amplification of canary traffic in certain low-volume regions and bursty client sessions. Current deterministic pin-by-session approaches either over-commit a session to a canary (risking poor UX) or under-commit it (losing signal for evaluation). Goals: 1) provide a probabilistic, thresholded session-affinity mechanism that leans sessions toward the target variant for X requests or Y minutes but gracefully decays based on entropy and regional capacity; 2) ensure routing decisions respect region-tier preferences and promote a predictable degrade path to fallback variants when capacity or latency SLOs are breached; 3) expose controls for PM to specify slice sizes, min-eval-exposure, and regional cutoffs.
acceptance_criteria: A1: New session-affinity policy can be enabled per route with parameters: exposure_threshold (requests), ttl_seconds, min_probability, max_probability, and regional_cutoff_latency_ms
A2: Sessions annotated with probabilistic pinning should maintain at least 75% assignment stability for the configured exposure_threshold in normal conditions

A3: In degraded-region scenarios (latency > regional_cutoff_latency_ms or capacity-saturated), sessions automatically fail over to the nearest compatible fallback variant and record a degrade reason metric
A4: Console UI shows per-route metrics for pinned-session fraction, average pin-duration, and regional failover counts for the rollout window
A5: End-to-end unit + integration tests simulate bursty sessions and verify TTL decay, probability recalculation, and fallback triggers
A6: Performance: introduced routing policy should add no more than 2ms median to route resolution in the 99th-percentile latency path when loaded
design_decisions: Use a hybrid deterministic-probabilistic scheme: deterministic assignment for the first request (for routing affinity), then probabilistic reinforcement for subsequent requests within exposure_threshold
Session keying: prefer stable session_id header; fall back to request cookie; if neither present, use short-lived ephemeral session hashed with client_ip and user_agent
Entropy budgeting: track a lightweight per-session entropy counter incremented on every route decision; entropy > H_THRESHOLD shifts probability toward default tier to avoid long-term skew
Regional cutoff heuristic: combine recent percentiles for p50/p95 latency and GPU utilization to detect degraded region; make cutoff configurable per deployment tier
Fallbacks: prefer variant-compatible fallbacks (same model family/quantization) to preserve API semantics; annotate logs with fallback_reason for postmortem analysis
implementation_notes: Add new RoutePolicy protobuf with fields: exposure_threshold:int, ttl_seconds:int, min_prob:float, max_prob:float, entropy_threshold:int, regional_cutoff_ms:int
Change router's resolve path: compute session_annotation -> check entropy and TTL -> compute assignment_probability -> consult capacity & latency probes -> finalize variant choice
Cache: store session pin metadata in the local in-memory LRU with write-through to Redis for cross-machine consistency in Dedicated deployments
Testing: harness script in infra/test-scenarios simulates 10k sessions with configurable burst patterns and region impairment
Backward compatibility: default policy must be identity with current pin semantics; rollout enablement gated by feature flag rollout:session_threshold_v1
risks: Risk: Redis write amplification under very high QPS if we persist every session decision; Mitigation: only persist when exposure_threshold > 1 or when cross-node consistency required
Risk: Increased route resolution CPU cost; Mitigation: precompute coarse-grained decisions for small requests and ensure fast path bypass for stateless calls
Risk: Incorrect fallback churn causing quality regressions; Mitigation: conservative default regional_cutoff_ms and canary-only enablement initially
Risk: Edge privacy concerns for session keying when falling back to client_ip; Mitigation: hash with salt and document in privacy review

notes_for_reviewers: Focus reviews on the entropy budgeting algorithm and Redis persistence heuristic. The perf spike on 95th latency was within acceptable bounds during our microbench, but we should validate at scale in staging before broad enablement. Also confirm that the fallback_reason tagging fits existing observability schemas.
